tasks.title: Opaque token issuance and revocable token store
tasks.description: Add POST /auth/login and POST /auth/logout. Issue a random 256-bit opaque token, store its SHA-256 hash in a local SQLite table with user_id and expiry. Logout deletes the row, which satisfies r2 (immediate revocation). No external identity provider, which satisfies r1.

tasks.title: Bearer-header auth middleware
tasks.description: Read the token from the Authorization: Bearer header, never a cookie, which satisfies r5. Resolve it through authenticate_user and attach the User to the request. Returns 401 on miss.

tasks.title: Scope note routes to the authenticated user
tasks.description: Apply the middleware to /notes and filter every query by request.user.id. Existing tests get an auth fixture rather than a rewrite, which satisfies r3.

interface_contracts.name: authenticate_user
interface_contracts.notes: Single lookup point. Returns None for unknown, expired, or revoked tokens — the middleware never inspects the token format itself, so t1 can change the storage scheme without touching t2.

interface_contracts.name: Authorization header format
interface_contracts.notes: Header only, no cookie fallback. Agreed as the resolution of r5 against r1.

interface_contracts.name: tokens
interface_contracts.signature: tokens(token_hash TEXT PRIMARY KEY, user_id INTEGER NOT NULL, expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL)
interface_contracts.notes: Local SQLite, same file as the existing notes DB. Indexed on token_hash, so the r6 sub-5ms budget holds for a single-node deploy.

concessions.accepted: Opaque tokens resolved against a local store
concessions.reason: r2 (immediate revocation) is a must-have for u1 and is not achievable with stateless JWT without a revocation list, which reintroduces the shared state that r4 was trying to avoid. gpt held r4's underlying goal — horizontal scale — and logged it as a deferred concern rather than a blocker, since the store is a single indexed table that can move to Redis later.
r5 (no cookies on mobile) is a must-have for u2. Cookies were claude's implementation preference, not a requirement u1 stated, so conceding it costs r1 and r2 nothing.
